title: Encoder-file changes are excluded from configuration rollback
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a failed auto-start writes the previous encoder settings file back before it says OBS was restored (VAL-118)', 'a setup that ends after the encoder settings file was written says when the file could not be put back (VAL-118)', 'a rollback that begins while the encoder settings file is being written does not claim it was restored (VAL-118)', and for the new transaction.registerUndo: 'registerUndo journals a step that is not an OBS request and undoes it in reverse order (VAL-118)', 'a registered undo that fails is named in the rollback failures, and the other steps still run (VAL-118)', 'a registered undo is dropped when it is released or the transaction commits, and cannot be added once it ended (VAL-118)', 'a registered undo still runs after the rollback could not confirm the stream stopped, while OBS requests are skipped (VAL-118)'; guard that passed before and after: 'a file write the server did not apply leaves nothing to put back (VAL-118)'
proof: Holds. configureObsStream wrote the encoder settings file through writeEncoderSettings (a call to the Nextra server, not an OBS request) and journaled nothing for it, so any later failure (a refused auto-start, a request that timed out, the setup deadline) restored the OBS settings and left the file as written, and an AV1 setup or a timeout still ended with 'OBS settings were restored'. The tests drive configureObsStream against fake OBS sockets with a writeEncoderSettings double that records every call. On the unchanged code: with a refused auto-start the double was called once (1 !== 2, 'the file is written once and restored once') and the message read 'OBS configured, but auto-start failed: output busy OBS settings were restored. Disable AV1 mode and retry to use H.264.'; with the colour space write left unanswered the message was 'OBS request SetProfileParameter timed out after 50ms. OBS settings were restored. Disable AV1 mode and retry to use H.264.' for every kind of file answer; with the deadline passing during the write it was 'OBS setup timed out after 300ms. OBS settings were restored. Disable AV1 mode and retry to use H.264.'; the four unit tests failed with 'transaction.registerUndo is not a function' (output kept in the scratchpad as obs-TASK-083-before.txt). Fix: createObsConfigurationTransaction gets registerUndo(label, undo), which journals a step that is no OBS request (hold and registerUndo share one journal function); a rollback calls undo() in its place in the reverse order, a throw or rejection is the failure '<label>: <message>', and the undo also runs when the stop gate ended the rollback for the OBS requests (a file is not changed under a live output, so skipping it gains nothing). configureObsStream writes the file through the new writeEncoderSettingsFile: it registers a note before the write that fails the rollback while the write is under way (a rollback that begins then, i.e. the deadline, cannot know what the file will hold, and the write may land afterwards), releases it when the answer comes, and after a write the server applied registers the real undo: when the answer carries `previous` (a non-empty settings object) the undo writes it back through writeEncoderSettings and fails with 'encoder settings file: not restored (<reason or error>)' if the server does not apply it or the call fails; without `previous` it fails with 'encoder settings file: not restored (its previous contents are not known)'. A write the server did not apply, or that threw, registers nothing, as before. Since the failures list is what the AV1/timeout 'OBS settings were restored' sentence depends on, that sentence is now emitted only when the file was restored too; otherwise the message ends 'Rollback incomplete: encoder settings file: ...'. Mutation checks: dropping the in-flight note, ignoring a refused restore, and skipping undos after a failed stop gate each fail one of the new tests. node --test tests/obsWebSocket.test.js tests/obsWebSocketWire.test.js 68/68, npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1218/1218) pass. Not done: the server never reports `previous` (lib/obsProfile.js and the obs-encoder-settings handler are out of scope by the prompt's constraints), so against the real server every failure after a successful file write now ends with 'Rollback incomplete: encoder settings file: not restored (its previous contents are not known)' instead of a false claim of restoration; a real restore needs writeStreamEncoderSettings to return what the file held and the handler to pass it on as `previous`.
